title: Cap. III Rej. Rat. 1: Bannes — common will only before sin / Adam intact
pass_a_gloss: Rejection. That common will of giving eternal life to all (as Bannes excellently) is conceived, according to our mode of understanding, before the foreknowledge of sin. Therefore it will avail only so far that from it it is proved that God in Adam intact willed the common salvation of all men, and to this end gave Adam sufficient means which, if he had willed to use them, he would have precipitated neither himself nor his posterity into the guilt of eternal death. But the fall of the first Adam having been posited, I deny that God ever had that common and indifferent will of giving eternal life to all in Christ Jesus.
pass_b_english: Rejection. That "common will to give eternal life to all" (Bannes is right) is only how we picture things before foreknowledge of sin. It proves at most that in intact Adam God willed everyone's salvation and gave him enough means — if Adam had used them, neither he nor his line would have fallen into eternal death's guilt. Once Adam fell, I deny God ever had a common, indifferent will to give eternal life to all in Christ Jesus.
source_text: Rej. Communis illa voluntas dandi vitam aeternam omnibus, (ut optime Bannes) secundum nostrum modum intelligendi concipitur ante praescientiam peccati. Eo igitur tantum valebit, ut inde probetur, Deum in Adamo integro voluisse communem omnium hominum salutem, atque in hunc finem dedisse Adamo sufficientia media, quibus si uti voluisset, neque seipsum, neque posteros in aeternae mortis reatum praecipitasset. Posito autem primi Adami lapsu, nego Deum unquam habuisse communem & indifferentem illam voluntatem dandi omnibus vitam aeternam in Christo Jesu.
